proposal.root_problem: Since gateway config change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on capture retries, gateway-timeout retries (stable at ~117-124/day) are sent to the PSP without an idempotency key; the PSP therefore executes them as new captures instead of deduplicating, producing real duplicate captures (0 before 09-09, 118-124/day after) and driving the double-charge ticket surge (9-11/week to 288-301/week).
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice.
symptoms: Orders with 2 captures jumped from 0 to 118-124/day starting 2026-09-09.
Double-charge support tickets surged from 9-11/week to 288-301/week while order volume stayed flat.
Customers are being genuinely double-charged on their statements, not just confused by pending vs. captured amounts.
causal_chain: Gateway timeouts during capture trigger automatic retries at a stable rate (~117-124/day), unchanged before and after 09-09 (F-02).
On 2026-09-09, SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on the gateway via config change CHG-77 for latency debugging, and it was never rolled back (F-03).
Before the change, all retries carried an idempotency key and the PSP deduplicated them, yielding 0 duplicate orders (F-04).
After the change, retries are sent with zero idempotency keys; the PSP processes each as a brand-new capture instead of deduplicating (F-05).
This produces real per-order duplicate captures starting exactly 09-09, matching the config-change date, not retry volume or user behavior (F-01).
The resulting genuine double charges drive support tickets from a 9-11/week baseline to 288-301/week in the same weeks (F-06).

proposal.summary: The customer-service request to build an apology-reply AI assistant (CL-01) was tested against evidence and rejected as the root cause (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP, REJECTED). Instead, the confirmed root problem (PD-1, H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED, CONFIRMED) is that gateway config change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries (E-02), causing the PSP to execute stable-volume gateway-timeout retries (E-01) as new captures instead of deduplicating them (E-03), producing real duplicate charges (0→118-124/day, E-01) and a ticket surge (9-11/week→288-301/week, E-05). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only the non-protected scope (verify current gateway setting, monitor duplicate-capture rate, monitor ticket volume) was released, while the protected action set_capture_idempotency was NOT executed because the unknown of whether the setting is still disabled today (VOB-U-CURRENT-SETTING-STATE) remains open and blocks that action from the release scope.
key_points: The initial requested solution was a complaint-reply drafting assistant (CL-01, SH-CS), but this framing was tested as hypothesis H-COMMUNICATION-GAP and REJECTED by evidence E-01 through E-06, which show a genuine payment-system defect rather than a reply-quality gap.

Root cause was established via a converging evidence chain: E-01 shows duplicate captures jumped from 0 to 118-124/day on 2026-09-09 while retry volume stayed flat; E-02 shows SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement that same day (CHG-77); E-03 shows all 242 post-change duplicates trace to retries sent without an idempotency key, versus 0 duplicates pre-change when all retries carried the key; E-05 shows the ticket surge timing matches.

Three alternative hypotheses (customer resubmission, handoff unreliability, perceived-not-actual duplication) were explicitly tested and REJECTED, each contradicted by E-01/E-02/E-03/E-04 (and E-05/E-06/E-08 for the perception hypothesis).

The release scope actually delivered covers only: verifying the current gateway setting against DA-CFG, monitoring the duplicate-capture rate via DA-CHG, and monitoring double-charge ticket volume via DA-TKT (solution_design SD-1 release_scope).

The protected action set_capture_idempotency (which would re-enable the fix, per runbook E-07 confirming it is reversible and requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation under constraint K-GW) was NOT executed in this release because VOB-U-CURRENT-SETTING-STATE is open and blocks it from release scope.
The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs; the release gate result is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items on hold.

4 orders are currently confirmed open and unrefunded with double captures (O-90211 $54.00, O-90244 $19.90, O-90302 $120.00, O-90318 $33.50; E-08), out of a broader estimated ~242+ affected orders since 2026-09-09 (E-03) for which no remediation workflow was executed in this release.
limitations_explained: The config fix itself was not executed in this release: re-enabling idempotency enforcement (set_capture_idempotency) is blocked because the open unknown U-CURRENT-SETTING-STATE/VOB-U-CURRENT-SETTING-STATE means it is unverified whether the setting is still disabled as of today (config-audit evidence E-02 only covers up to 2026-09-10).

The approximately 242+ orders already double-charged since 2026-09-09 (per E-03) are not remediated by anything released; a separate refund/remediation workflow would be needed, and the release-provided data lists no refund tool or authorization as currently existing for this.

Data completeness for payments-db, psp-logs, config-audit and crm-tickets is marked UNKNOWN (unknown U-DATA-COMPLETENESS, open; VOB-R-3 open and required before production), so it is not established whether the monitored metrics (M-DUP-CAPTURE-RATE, M-DUP-TICKET-RATE) cover all orders/regions.
The gateway-config tool's health is UNKNOWN (runtime.tool_health), so the reliability of any live-state verification of the gateway setting is uncertain.
The DEFINE gate itself only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before this release.

Note: the state data shows an internal inconsistency — the released limitations list states remediation of affected orders is blocked because VOB-U-AFFECTED-CUSTOMER-REMEDIATIO is open, while the verification_obligations and unknowns records elsewhere mark that same VOB and unknown as RESOLVED; this discrepancy is reported as-is rather than resolved here.
